headline: Big Bend Backcountry and Chisos Basin Reservations
reservation: Book Chisos Mountains Lodge through the lodge concessioner and reservable NPS campgrounds through Recreation.gov; check current closures and availability before planning a stay. Backcountry camping requires a separate permit obtained in person or online depending on the specific zone. Entry fees are per vehicle and valid for seven days; always check the official NPS site for changing river crossing statuses and trail closures due to heat or maintenance.

days.title: Canyons and Desert Drives

stops.name: Ross Maxwell Scenic Drive
stops.detail: Drive this 30-mile route to see the Sotol Vista and volcanic formations of the Chihuahuan Desert.

stops.name: Santa Elena Canyon
stops.detail: Walk to the water's edge where 1,500-foot limestone walls tower over the Rio Grande.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the round trip drive plus stops; roads are paved but winding.
days.note: Santa Elena trail access may be restricted during Rio Grande flooding events.

days.title: High Elevation Mountain Escape

stops.name: Lost Mine Trail
stops.detail: A steady climb through juniper and oaks offering views of Casa Grande and the Pine Canyon.

stops.name: Window View Trail
stops.detail: An easy paved path leading to a dramatic mountain notch overlooking the desert below.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes from the park entrance to the Chisos Basin; steep grades apply.
days.note: Chisos Basin parking frequently fills by 9 AM during peak spring weeks.

days.title: Fossil History and Rio Grande Views

stops.name: Fossil Discovery Exhibit
stops.detail: Explore the park's 130-million-year geologic history at this open-air shaded pavilion.

stops.name: Boquillas Canyon Overlook
stops.detail: View the massive cliffs of the eastern park section where the river cuts through the mountains.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for transit between the Fossil Exhibit and Boquillas area.
days.note: Check the Boquillas Port of Entry official hours if planning a legal international crossing.

intel.title: Basin Constraints
intel.text: Large RVs are restricted on the winding road into Chisos Basin. Parking for standard cars is extremely limited at the Lost Mine trailhead.

intel.title: Remote Desert Safety
intel.text: Cell service is unavailable in most of the park, including Santa Elena and Boquillas. Download offline maps and notify others of your planned return time.

intel.title: Station Distances
intel.text: Fuel is only available at Panther Junction and Rio Grande Village within the park. Ensure a full tank before leaving gateway towns like Alpine or Marathon.

intel.title: Heat Management
intel.text: Midday temperatures in the desert sections often exceed safe hiking levels from May to September. Complete lower-elevation walks before 10 AM.

intel.title: Unpaved Route Warning
intel.text: Old Maverick Road is an improved dirt road usually passable for most vehicles when dry, but it can become impassable after rain. Check current conditions, separate River Road requirements, and rental restrictions before driving either route.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at Midland (MAF). Drive 5 hours south, stopping for groceries in Alpine, as services inside the park are very limited.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance vehicles are strongly recommended for desert exploration; check rental contracts for off-pavement restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: The Window View Trail is a classic location for sunset, though mountain peaks may obscure light earlier than expected.
